topic: Wild lion populations by country: Tanzania ~17,200 (TAWIRI national census 2024/25), South Africa 3,284, Kenya 2,515; Africa total ~22,000–25,000 (IUCN Cat Specialist Group 2025); lions occupy ~6% of historic range; India's Gir landscape 891 Asiatic lions (2025 census)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Kenya or South Africa, the famous safari destinations, have the most lions.
myths.reality: Tanzania's 2024/25 national census counted about 17,200 lions; South Africa follows with 3,284 and Kenya with 2,515.

landscape.our_gap: Lion Shorts are hunt clips and roar compilations; nobody plays the population map — three safari countries, the counts, how little range is left, and the single Indian forest outside Africa.

citizen_tz.title: Tanzania emerges as the top in lion and buffalo populations
citizen_tz.notes: TAWIRI 2024/25 census: Tanzania ≈ 17,200 lions; South Africa 3,284; Botswana 3,064; Kenya 2,515; Zambia 2,349

cat_tz.title: Wildlife census shows Tanzania leads world in lion populations
cat_tz.notes: TAWIRI census 2024/25: 17,200 lions, highest recorded by any country; 18.1% outside protected areas

iucn_lion.title: Panthera leo
iucn_lion.notes: Vulnerable; population decreasing; IUCN Cat Specialist Group 2025 estimate 22,000–25,000 adult and subadult lions in Africa

aa_lions.title: FACTBOX — World Lion Day: How many lions remain in the wild?
aa_lions.notes: Lion Recovery Fund ≈ 23,000 wild lions in Africa (African Lion Database); IUCN Cat SG 22,000–25,000 in 2025

tt_range.title: World Lion Day: Only around 23,000 lions remain in wild across Africa
tt_range.notes: IUCN Cat Specialist Group: lions occupied 566,675 km² in 2025 = 6.13% of historical range

animalmap.title: Lion 2025: facts, habitat, population
animalmap.notes: IUCN Cat SG 22,000–25,000 in Africa; Tanzania census 2024/25 ≈ 17,200; India 891 Asiatic lions (2025 census)

wiki_asiatic.title: Asiatic lion
wiki_asiatic.notes: May 2025 survey: 891 lions across 35,000 km² of Gujarat (394 in Gir NP and adjoining areas); the only wild lions outside Africa

natgeo_gir.title: Can India's last lions be saved?
natgeo_gir.notes: 2025 census: 891 Asiatic lions; Gir, Gujarat, the last wild lions outside Africa

gujarat_fd.title: 16th Lion Population Estimation, May 2025
gujarat_fd.notes: 891 Asiatic lions estimated across 35,000 km² of the Gir landscape in May 2025 (674 in 2020)

claims.text: Tanzania has the most wild lions of any country: about 17,200 in the 2024/25 TAWIRI national census, more than all other countries combined (Africa ≈ 22,000–25,000).
vo: where do most of the world's wild lions live
tanzania. its latest count found some 17,000 lions, more than all the other countries on earth put together

claims.text: South Africa has about 3,284 lions and Kenya 2,515 (same census comparison); Africa holds roughly 22,000–25,000 wild lions (IUCN Cat SG 2025; Lion Recovery Fund ≈ 23,000).
vo: south africa has some 3,000 and kenya even fewer. all of africa holds just 23,000 wild lions

claims.text: Lions occupy only about 6% of their historical range (IUCN Cat Specialist Group 2025: 6.13%), i.e. they have vanished from about 94% of it.
vo: lions have now gone from 94 percent of all the land they once roamed

claims.text: The only wild lions outside Africa are the Asiatic lions of the Gir landscape in Gujarat, India: 891 in the 2025 census.
vo: outside africa, only gir, in india, still has any at all: nearly 900 asiatic lions, and nowhere else
